scope: Independent final Web retained-image resolver/Canvas/prefix/Three review plus cross-reviewed whole-player startup completion follow-up.

findings.problem: Zero-eligible, partial or target-mismatch fallback retained old GPU instance/definition owners.
findings.disposition: Corrected: clear/reconcile selected GPU ownership, then sweep only actually selected generations. Focused regression source reviewed.

findings.problem: Canvas.ready waiter could remain stranded after asset invalidation retired its pending generation.
findings.disposition: Corrected: reconcile current required asset generations and notify; stale old loads cannot unblock current readiness.

findings.problem: Three would silently resize oversized source images and change crop interiors.
findings.disposition: Corrected: source admission requires a known positive actual GPU maxTextureSize and supported image dimensions; otherwise Canvas fallback.

findings.problem: Boot READY could precede Canvas assets, or become stale when a cursor became required at the final RAF barrier.
findings.disposition: Root delegated main/helper/cursor implementation to this reviewer; independently cross-reviewed by Codex /root/runtime_audit. Startup awaits renderer/Canvas/current cursor readiness, redraws at final commit and requires complete host outcomes; unknown outcomes fail explicitly.

result: Corrections re-read; no additional concrete P1/P2 in bounded reviewed scope.

evidence.scope: Fractional pan/zoom/clip, DPR/portrait, source crop/alpha/order, large origin and context restore. Accepted outer one-pixel coverage rim can differ from Canvas AA.

limits: The prefix accelerates only a leading eligible image-batch run; it preserves ordinary Canvas HUD/interleaving and falls back for unsupported precision, transforms, image limits or targets.
GPU pixel-center outer edge coverage intentionally differs from Canvas AA. Interior tolerances are bounded by tested fixtures, not universal pixel equivalence.

This record is not the final SDK/runtime artifact manifest, full-game rendering acceptance, FPS/GC benchmark or universal memory-leak certification. GPU allocation errors use fatal host teardown; no recoverable driver-allocation transaction is claimed.
